title: Respect browser, account and staff consent in analytics collection

source.ref: Owner analytics dashboard and user-flow request, 2026-11-13.

detail: Consenting browser activity is collected only after trusted audience resolution; client-supplied GA identity and authority flags cannot bypass the public collector. Identity comes from browser cookies, and private URL/title content is removed. New focused regressions failed before implementation; existing probes were preserved. Implementation proof does not assert production activation. CI trace 43522750456 identified excessive generic instantiation in the existing gems RPC bind, blocking this release under the unchanged 6144 MB heap. Moving its existing exact RPC signature before bind preserves the call and reduces targeted compiler instantiations from 3536235 to 7924 (heap 540 MB to 146 MB); no probe, test or memory budget changed. The same generated generic bind remained at other callers, so the admin client now explicitly types receiver-only RPC binding as preserving the original full SDK signature. Three targeted consumers drop from 3597768 to 69469 compiler instantiations (646 MB to 436 MB); direct and bound RPC names and required arguments remain checked, and emitted JavaScript is identical. The complete remaining bind inventory found twelve admin-client sites covered centrally, two generated-schema session-client sites in message readers, one type-erased ticket client and one already-narrow test client. The session factory now preserves the same receiver-only binding identity too; targeted message-reader instantiations fall from 3597626 to 69415 for the first reader, with both readers and factory checked cleanly. Cookie and bearer behavior emit byte-identical JavaScript; direct and bound RPC validation remains strict.
